executive_summary: Across Q1–Q3 FY26, M&B Engineering delivered strong revenue growth, driven by export scaling (US, Canada) and a robust domestic order book, while navigating tariff-led margin volatility. Management consistently emphasized disciplined growth, capacity-led execution, and margin protection over aggressive topline chasing. Guidance on FY26 revenue (~₹1,225–1,250 cr) and EBITDA margin (~12.75–13%) has remained largely stable, with delivery tracking expectations so far. Key themes include export-led margin uplift, capacity constraints at Sanand, gradual Cheyyar ramp-up, and cautious optimism amid tariff and FX headwinds.

evidence.statement: We are targeting an overall topline growth of over 25% in FY 2026… confident of further improving our EBITDA margins in FY 2026.
We remain very much confident of achieving the overall topline of 25% growth in the current fiscal… EBITDA around 13% on a full year basis.
We expect the topline to be around INR 1,250 crores with EBITDA margin in the visibility of 12.75%… supported by a strong Q4.
We don’t want to overcommit… we will be in a better position to provide more specific guidance for FY27 at Q4.

guidance_evolution.pattern_summary: Management sets achievable targets, revises margins prudently when conditions change, and avoids aggressive over-guidance.

margin_commentary: Margins have been a central discussion point, with management consistently attributing pressure to US sectoral tariffs (50%), FX volatility on Proflex imports, and export freight costs. While export EBITDA remains structurally higher than domestic, management admitted to absorbing some tariffs to build US relationships. Credibility is supported by clear quantification of tariff impact (e.g., ₹2.85 cr in Q2FY26) and realistic full-year EBITDA guidance of ~12.75–13%.
revenue_growth_narrative: Revenue growth is largely organic, driven by strong order inflows in Phenix (PEB) and Proflex roofing, with exports emerging as a key incremental driver. Management consistently cited industrial capex, railways, agri-warehousing, and North American demand as growth drivers. The narrative has remained consistent, with capacity ramp-up (Cheyyar) and brownfield expansions underpinning medium-term growth.
